base_rationale: The branch's PREVIOUS HEAD, i.e. the code the round-2 review was written against. The branch parent df4b24a is the wrong base for this round: the round-1 commit introduced resolve_ollama_host, so the new tests collect with an ImportError there and prove nothing. Verified that df4b24a produces exactly that ImportError before switching.
reproduced_before_fixing: Yes, both findings, on the real CLI construction path. PipelineConfig(qwen_backend='vllm', qwen_vllm_url='http://gpu-node.cluster:8000/v1') -> UnifiedPipeline(cfg)._probe_backend_idle() called probe_ollama_idle('http://localhost:11434'). resolve_ollama_host('::1') -> 'http://::1'.

findings.summary: A configured vLLM backend is still probed at Ollama localhost on the real CLI path; qwen_vllm_url ignored and the CLI never assigns backend_probe.
findings.how: Which server is asked now follows qwen_backend through a new OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BACKENDS frozenset in socr/tables/extract.py — the SAME predicate make_table_reader already uses to pick the crop reader, shared rather than duplicated so probe and reader cannot drift into asking about different machines. vLLM/SGLang is probed at {qwen_vllm_url}/models via a new probe_openai_server_idle; /api/tags is Ollama's and a vLLM server 404s it, which reads as dead, so fixing the host without the endpoint would have relocated the defect. backend_probe stays as an override seam but the default path no longer depends on a caller assigning it. New test test_probe_and_crop_reader_agree_on_which_server_to_ask walks all six backend spellings.
findings.deliberate_limit: qwen_backend='auto' still probes Ollama. Everywhere else in this codebase auto resolves to a local Ollama daemon (make_table_reader sends its crops there), so that is the correct answer for auto; inferring vLLM from a non-default qwen_vllm_url alone would make the probe disagree with the reader, which is the class of bug being fixed. The reviewer's repro snippet set only qwen_vllm_url; the real defect is the qwen_backend='vllm' deployment and that is what is fixed. Stated explicitly in the PR body.

findings.summary: A bare unbracketed IPv6 host resolves to the invalid http://::1.
findings.how: _bracket_bare_ipv6 brackets a host token holding more than one colon and not already bracketed (one colon is a port), applied BEFORE the port default. Measured that this was worse than reported: at a157f76, OLLAMA_HOST=::1 made probe_ollama_idle RAISE httpx.InvalidURL ('Invalid port: :1') — InvalidURL is NOT an httpx.HTTPError, it is raised while building the request — straight out of the cascade-halt guard, losing the document over a typo in an env var. Both probes now catch it via a named _PROBE_ERRORS tuple and answer 'not idle'. Verified: same command returns False on the branch. All the other shapes the reviewer asked for are a parametrised table: explicit port, scheme present, trailing slash, blank/whitespace, bracketed and unbracketed IPv6, an IPv6 zone id, and the bare-host case whose port default must not regress (it did not).

findings.summary: test_trigger_predicate_unchanged pins source text, not trigger behaviour; a second condition bypassing the predicate would still pass.
findings.how: Kept the spelling pin as a cheap tripwire and added test_probe_is_consulted_only_after_a_timeout, which drives the real process() cascade-halt path and asserts the probe is consulted AND the PARTIAL_SAVE_VLM_TIMEOUT halt fires iff an attempt's reason contains 'timeout'. Reuses PP-2's existing cascade-halt fixture rather than building a second one that could drift; patches _available_engines_for_agentic for CI hermeticity. _had_timeout itself is untouched.

findings.summary: The crop-timeout cascade probe in extract.py had the same defect in miniature: VllmTableReader.host is its /v1 base URL and was being asked for /api/tags.
findings.how: New _probe_reader_idle picks the endpoint from the reader type. The result only enriches a log line (degradation there is unconditional), but a log line naming a hardware failure that never happened is what #222 was filed about. Small and in #222's scope ('which machine is asked').

not_touched_on_purpose: _had_timeout — its all-attempts scan and bare-substring 'timeout' match are #222's defects 2 and 3, deferred to #221/#227. test_trigger_predicate_unchanged still pins it.

The module-level probe_ollama_idle indirection in _probe_backend_idle. Five test files patch socr.pipeline.orchestrator.probe_ollama_idle; routing around it would leave those patches silently ineffective. Added test_existing_module_level_patches_still_reach_the_probe so a future cleanup fails loudly. All five files re-run green: 171 passed, 2 xfailed.
closes_222_note: Stated in the PR body: this fixes which machine is asked, not what the probe can detect. A /api/tags or /models ping still answers while the GPU is wedged; that is #221/#227.

base_run.non_behavioural_note: test_probe_and_crop_reader_agree_on_which_server_to_ask fails with ImportError for OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BACKENDS, a symbol this change introduces. It is a structural anti-drift guard for the new mechanism and cannot behave at a commit where the mechanism does not exist. NOT counted as proof; the blocking finding is proved by the two tests above it, which name nothing new.
